**The paper does not report an NDCG@10 figure for GenRec or for the production ranker.** The only offline ranking metric it reports is Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR).

What the paper does report for the offline comparison:

- **Lift over production:** GenRec achieves about **+1.6% relative MRR** over the production baseline. It does this with roughly **40× fewer Phase-2 labeled training examples** and fewer input signals (p. 6).
- **Further scaling:** Offline metrics keep improving as training data and input signals are scaled up (p. 6).
- **Baseline:** The production model is "a mature discriminative model tuned over many years" (p. 6).

Other offline results, all measured in MRR:

- MRR rises steadily as Phase-2 training data grows from 1× to 20×, for both the ~1B and ~10B models (pp. 6–7, Figure 4).
- Phase-1 training gives about a 10–20% MRR gain over an off-the-shelf model. Phase-2 training gives a further 35–50% gain (p. 7, Table 1).
